page: Microsoft Azure D64as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv5 server family. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with x86_64 architecture, this instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and is supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is highly efficient, highlighted by a top-tier Passmark memory score in the top 10% and strong cached read-only memory bandwidth. However, uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths fall into the average category. Single-core performance is moderately balanced, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression tests registering average results.

The D64as_v5 is well-suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, database operations, and Redis deployments, where it demonstrates strong throughput. It also handles small to medium language model inference tasks effectively, though performance drops to average levels for larger 70B models. Given the absence of bundled local storage, users must factor in external storage configurations. This instance offers a balanced resource density, making it a cost-efficient option for general-purpose enterprise applications and multi-threaded processing without the premium cost of specialized memory or GPU hardware.
